description: HydroConDams compiles and corrects available dam datasets so that macro-scale hydrologic models can route and store water through reservoirs consistently with their river networks. For each reservoir it gives the location of the single major outflow point, maximum capacity, inundated surface area, upstream catchment area, construction year and primary purpose. The University of New Hampshire's Water Systems Analysis Group produced it; coverage is the Conterminous United States in version 1, and version 2.0 (2021) adds global data including 27 large lakes from the Global Lake and Wetland Database. It is available as a free download from Harvard Dataverse as tab-delimited files with PDF metadata, under CC0 with some additional terms. Caveats: the authors say it suits meso- to macro-scale models only and is not suitable for individual structures, structural integrity, flood risk or any assessment of risk to life or property, and no accuracy is guaranteed. Simulation uses: reservoir storage and routing in regional water-resource network models and climate adaptation runs. Related records: the US National Inventory of Dams (data-usace-national-inventory-of-dams) and GRanD (data-grand-global-reservoir-and-dam-database).
